title: I barely marketed my first Steam game and somehow reached 221 wishlists
author: Just_Paterek
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/3lnj4dcttdkh1.png?width=882&format=png&auto=webp&s=239fb3488fbacfb631041b9f94bf57089b8c76e0

  
  
Less than a month after release, and the Steam page itself has only been live for around two weeks.

So far: 221 wishlists, 18 sales and basically no real marketing.

I'm not traditionally a game developer, so AI became a pretty important part of my workflow while building Cyber Plinko. I mainly used it to help me prototype ideas faster, work through Unity/code problems, review solutions and iterate when I got stuck.

One thing I learned pretty quickly though: AI can help you build much faster, but it doesn't solve the hard part of actually getting people to care about the game.

I spent most of my time developing instead of making videos, contacting creators or properly marketing it.

The numbers are obviously small, but seeing people I don't know wishlist and actually buy something I built still feels great.

For anyone else developing with AI: has it changed where you spend most of your time? For me, development became faster, but marketing has now become the bottleneck.

The game is Cyber Plinko, a Plinko roguelite currently in Early Access. [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4735700/Cyber\_Plinko/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4735700/Cyber_Plinko/)
